extras.verified_at_basis: the turbobit.net home page states the total volume and number of files are unlimited
extras.quota_verbatim: Unlimited total: 'The total volume and number of your files are unlimited'. Free unregistered uploads are capped at 200 MB; registered free accounts go much higher (operator advertises up to 100 GB file transfer volume).
extras.limits_verbatim: Registered free: file size ceiling well above 200 MB (unregistered 200 MB). Retention: files expire after inactivity ('storage time expiration' is a listed deletion reason). Free download ~5 GB/day, 55-60 KB/s class throttling on the sister host. Turbo 40 GB/day, 600 GB/month.
extras.egress_verbatim: Free downloads: ~5 GB/day per user with a hard speed cap and IP queueing. Turbo: 40 GB/day and 600 GB/month. No per-GB price.
extras.chaining_verbatim: Unlimited total per account is the headline; with email-only registration the chain is N accounts. The 40 GB/day cap is per *download* identity, so serving volume scales with IPs, not accounts.
extras.tooling_verbatim: Turbobit Uploader desktop app, FTP upload, and third-party rclone/JDownloader support; no first-party public REST API documented.
extras.agent_focus: regional and non-English large-file hosts, especially very large single-file caps with no total-storage limit

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
